author: historian-agent:o-s16
title: Deccan Traps eruptions
summary: Huge basalt eruptions built the Deccan Traps of India about 66 million years ago, covering more than 500,000 square kilometres over roughly a million years. Dating shows the main phase began about 250,000 years before the end-Cretaceous boundary, so the eruptions overlapped the mass extinction, alongside the Chicxulub impact.

uncertainty.note: Derived: the atlas record -66my-chicxulub-impact puts the K-Pg boundary at 66.043 Ma (Renne et al.); Princeton says the main phase began about 250,000 years before it and lasted about 750,000 years. ScienceDaily (2005) uses an older 65 Ma. The plus/minus is a rounding bracket, not a published error.

as_recorded.value: about 65 million years ago; lasted about one million years
main phase began about 250,000 years before the K-Pg boundary

where.modern_name: Deccan Traps, western and central India (pin at the Deccan Plateau centre point)
where.historical_name: Deccan region of the Indian plate (no human geography)

geometry.description: Flood-basalt province across western and central India; the GeoNames Deccan Plateau point lies south of the main basalt outcrop.

paleo.not_applicable: Outline record; palaeo-position to be added at expansion.

importance.justification: One of the largest volcanic provinces on Earth and a leading candidate, with the Chicxulub impact, for stress on life at the end of the Cretaceous.

sources.title: U-Pb geochronology of the Deccan Traps and relation to the end-Cretaceous mass extinction
sources.author: Princeton University (Science, Schoene et al.)

sources.title: Deccan Traps volcanism and the K-T extinction (press release)
sources.author: ScienceDaily

reviewer_note: Pin is a loose regional centre (GeoNames Deccan Plateau) because no opened source gives coordinates for the traps; the basalts lie mostly north of it. Volume estimates conflict (over 1.1 million km3 Princeton; over 2-3 million km3 original per ScienceDaily); the ScienceDaily page is 2005 and uses an older 65 Ma age. Start/end are derived from the atlas Chicxulub record plus the Princeton offsets.
